page: Amazon Web Services m5d.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

A key hardware feature of the m5d.xlarge is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. This local storage provides low-latency, direct-attached disk access compared to network-attached alternatives. The instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the m5d.xlarge demonstrates modest performance characteristics. Its CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, falls into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth for large blocks and cryptographic operations are positioned in the weak category. However, its PassMark memory score achieves an average rating, landing in the middle 50% of tested systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5d.xlarge offers a balanced resource profile, combining dedicated compute, standard DDR4 memory density, and local NVMe storage without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. It is appropriate for general-purpose workloads that benefit from local scratch space or caching, such as light web serving, development environments, small database instances, and basic data processing tasks.
